title: Chard and courgette frittata with toasted seeds

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Eggs, fresh vegetables, cheese, seeds, oil and herbs are all plain whole foods a grandparent would keep.

supermarket.reason: Every item, including chard, vegetarian hard cheese and pumpkin seeds, is an everyday mainstream supermarket line.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded non-stick frying pan and a grater, and covering the pan to set a frittata is a beginner technique.

works.reason: Eight eggs with about 600g of vegetables makes a properly set frittata for four, and the low, covered cook of 12 to 15 minutes suits it.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers the grating and chopping, which can overlap the frying, and the 15-minute cook matches the covered setting time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including mint and lemon zest, appears in the steps and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm chard and courgette frittata suits an early-June lunch, and the chard is a main vegetable rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: Short, clear British English steps with no restaurant jargon or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Eggs, cheese, seeds and plenty of greens make a satisfying, protein-rich family lunch.
